title: Freeport Indonesia to wrap up Gresik plant repairs by early September

title: Indonesia Aims to Dominate Global Nickel Supply Chain Amid Smelter Expansion and Import Challenges
body: APNI’s Meidy Katrin Lengkey highlighted Indonesia’s 54 operational smelters and 49 under construction, with a 414,000‑ton consumption base and a 700‑million‑ton smelter demand, positioning the country to become a global nickel hub, while noting challenges from raw‑material shortages and reliance on Philippine imports for magnesium‑rich nickel. She warned of a shift from a three‑year RKAB to a one‑year plan, forecasted nickel prices at $15,000–$16,000 next year, and urged government action to keep costs competitive and support the domestic battery and stainless‑steel industry.

title: Indonesia Nickel Mining Industry Discusses Flexibility of B40 Biodiesel Program Amid Rising Costs and Supply Delays
body: The Indonesian government, led by the EBTKE, convened a forum to evaluate the 40% biodiesel (B40) mandate, noting that the policy adds 3–5% to nickel mining production costs while nickel prices have fallen to about Rp15,000 per ton. Stakeholders called for a flexible, quarterly review and stronger supply guarantees to mitigate the impact of B40 and prepare for the upcoming B50 requirement.
